html:
A Latin epic poem by Virgil, written between 29 and 19 BCE, telling how the Trojan hero Aeneas escaped the fall of Troy and came to Italy, where his descendants would found Rome.

Its twelve books copy the two poems of Homer. The first six are a journey like the Odyssey. Aeneas is shipwrecked at Carthage, where Queen Dido falls in love with him; when he leaves on the gods' orders she kills herself and curses his people, a mythic origin for the Punic Wars. In book six he goes down to the underworld and sees the souls of future Romans, ending with Augustus. The last six books are a war in Italy like the Iliad, ending when Aeneas kills his enemy Turnus.

The poem glorifies Rome and Augustus, whose family, the Julii, claimed descent from Aeneas's son, yet it is full of sorrow at the price of empire. Virgil died before he could finish revising it and asked for it to be burned. Augustus had it published.

It became Rome's national poem and the core of Latin schooling. In the Divine Comedy, Dante takes Virgil as his guide through Hell.
sum: A Latin epic poem by Virgil, written between 29 and 19 BCE, telling how the Trojan hero Aeneas escaped the fall of Troy and came to Italy, where his descendants would found Rome.
